unit.title: Hotbeds and coldframes
unit.needIt: Hotbeds let you grow food earlier than your neighbors by creating a tiny summer inside a box. It helps you get a head start on your garden even when the ground is still frozen.
unit.why: A gardener wants to grow lettuce before everyone else. They build a box with glass and use rotting manure to create a steady heat source. This box acts like a tiny greenhouse that mimics summer weather in the middle of winter.
unit.outcome: Build a hotbed to start seeds early in the season.
unit.reachesYou: You might see these wooden boxes in a backyard or a local nursery. You will use this idea when you want to grow plants that need warmth but the weather is still cold.
unit.do: Find a sunny spot in your yard and look at how much heat a glass window can trap from the sun.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of a hotbed?
quiz.why: The text says a hotbed is a place where summer conditions can be imitated by supplying steady heat.
quiz.quote: It is simply making a place in which summer conditions can be imitated by supplying it with steady, gentle heat, and in confining this heat within an inclosure.

quiz.q: What material is generally used to generate heat?
quiz.why: The lecture states that fresh manure from a horse-stable is the common heat source.
quiz.quote: The heat-generating material is generally fresh manure from the horse-stable, or a mixture of that and coarse litter.

quiz.q: How deep should the heat-generating material be?
quiz.why: The text specifies that there should be at least a foot and a half of this material.
quiz.quote: There should be at least a foot and a half of this heat-generating material.

quiz.q: Which direction should a hotbed face for the best results?
quiz.why: Facing south allows the hotbed to take the most advantage of the sunshine.
quiz.quote: The best location for a hotbed is one facing the south, that all possible advantage can. be taken of sunshine

quiz.q: What must be done to ensure plants stay healthy?
choices: Give them plenty of fresh air
quiz.why: Plants need fresh air to grow vigorously and avoid becoming weak.
quiz.quote: In it plants will grow healthily and vigorously, provided they are given plenty of fresh air.

quiz.q: What temperature should the hotbed reach before seeding?
quiz.why: The text says the bed is ready for seeding when the thermometer hits 85 or 90 degrees.
quiz.quote: When it registers 85° or 90° the bed is ready for seeding.

partials: It uses manure to make heat.
It uses glass to trap that heat.
It needs fresh air to stay healthy.
It gives plants an early start.
crystal.key: A hotbed is a glass enclosure that uses fermenting manure to create a warm summer environment for early plants.

decoys.text: A hotbed is a self-regulating system.
decoys.why: The text says it is not a self-regulating thing and needs frequent attention.

decoys.text: You should keep the sash closed all day.
decoys.why: The text says you must lift the sash to provide fresh air.

crystal.aha: By trapping heat from manure inside a glass box, you create a controlled summer for your plants.
